rendered:
The question rests on a wrong premise: the paper does not pick that value as the optimum for the boronic acid ligand (BA). It picks 165 μM[1]. The number 120 μM[2] is only the top of the first concentration range they tested.

This is how they got to their choice:
1. They first raised the BA concentration from 0 to 120 μM[3], and the CD signal of BA@L-HGNRs after redispersion in NH4HCO3 buffer went up clearly over that range (a prominent enhancement of the 600 nm CD signal was observed[4]).
2. Time-dependent CD and UV–vis tests showed that the 165 μM 4-MPBA-derived BA@L-HGNRs showing exceptional spectral stability during the entire monitoring process[5]. This confirmed that the BA coating made the particles redisperse more stably.
3. Raising the concentration further, up to 225 μM resulted in only marginal changes in the CD signal[6]. The CD intensity reached its maximum at 165 μM, after which it exhibited a slight decrease at higher concentrations[7].
4. So they chose 165 μM was chosen as the optimized condition for all subsequent experiments[8].

The paper's reason for optimizing the BA concentration at all is that how well the probe disperses depends on how much of its surface the BA covers. That coverage in turn affects how the probe interacts with bacterial surfaces (closely related to BA surface coverage[9]).

The other place this value appears is the cysteine range (45 to 120 μM[10]). That is about cysteine, not BA, and the cysteine optimum there was 75 μM[11].
